### 21. Neon Clay — complete proposed implementation design (`R09-G21`)
**Source:** `G180`, source `Inherited original 200; previously scored`, conceptual score **92.75 /100**, proposed upfront price **$2.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Press and split neon clay masses to match an expressive sculpture. **Signature animated environment:** SDF metaball sculpting, normal-estimated glossy materials and 3D voxel outlines. **Core abstraction:** radiance-routing field.
#### 5.21.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees sdf metaball sculpting, normal-estimated glossy materials and 3d voxel outlines, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Press and split neon clay masses to match an expressive sculpture. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `radiance-routing field` computational rules, visual `SDF metaball sculpting, normal-estimated glossy materials and 3D voxel outlines` and player control arrangement `Existing concept input requires game-specific design verification`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.21.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** color_{t+1}=M(control,geometry) color_t; clamp radiance and preserve bounded signal energy. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Press and split neon clay masses to match an expressive sculpture. Normalize input into `NeonClayAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** route an emissive signature into target gates without contaminating disallowed bins. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 6 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** discrete path BFS plus RGB-signature conservation assertions. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** color-only puzzles, radiance overflows, near-black legibility. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.21.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting SDF metaball sculpting, normal-estimated glossy materials and 3D voxel outlines; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable radiance-routing field handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with press and split neon clay masses to match an expressive sculpture; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative radiance-routing field predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Existing concept input requires game-specific design verification. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.21.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** additive beam meshes, prismatic material and analytic color diffusion. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** SDF metaball sculpting, normal-estimated glossy materials and 3D voxel outlines. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `NeonClayScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `NeonClayParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `133eb22f0069` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.21.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct radiance-routing field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct radiance-routing field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct radiance-routing field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct radiance-routing field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct radiance-routing field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct radiance-routing field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct radiance-routing field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct radiance-routing field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct radiance-routing field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct radiance-routing field controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

### 22. Ringworld Courier — complete proposed implementation design (`R09-G22`)
**Source:** `G253`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **92.74 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Dock a glowing capsule by synchronizing motion with rotating rings. **Signature animated environment:** reflective ring structures and atmospheric edge glow; Numerical gravitation in fixed steps, analytic orbit curves, procedural planets and starfields. **Core abstraction:** deterministic orbit engine.
#### 5.22.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees reflective ring structures and atmospheric edge glow; numerical gravitation in fixed steps, analytic orbit curves, procedural planets and starfields, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Dock a glowing capsule by synchronizing motion with rotating rings. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `deterministic orbit engine` computational rules, visual `reflective ring structures and atmospheric edge glow; Numerical gravitation in fixed steps, analytic orbit curves, procedural planets and starfields` and player control arrangement `Tune gravitation and launch windows to achieve stable goals`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.22.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** dr/dt=v, dv/dt=Σ GM_i (r_i-r)/|r_i-r|³; use semi-implicit fixed integrator. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Dock a glowing capsule by synchronizing motion with rotating rings. Normalize input into `RingworldCourierAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** design stable orbital transfers/alignments without collision. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 5 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** bounded launch-window sampling and state-integrity/fuel constraints. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** numerical drift, interactions too fine for touch. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.22.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting reflective ring structures and atmospheric edge glow; Numerical gravitation in fixed steps, analytic orbit curves, procedural planets and starfields; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable deterministic orbit engine handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with dock a glowing capsule by synchronizing motion with rotating rings; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative deterministic orbit engine predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Tune gravitation and launch windows to achieve stable goals. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.22.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** procedural glowing orbits, planet spheres and gravitational field ribbons. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** reflective ring structures and atmospheric edge glow; Numerical gravitation in fixed steps, analytic orbit curves, procedural planets and starfields. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `RingworldCourierScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `RingworldCourierParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `00cb96e05fa8` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.

Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

#### 5.22.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** numerical drift, interactions too fine for touch. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `reflective ring structures and atmospheric edge glow; Numerical gravitation in fixed steps, analytic orbit curves, procedural planets and starfields` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND9_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round9/ringworld-courier/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. ### 23. Biolume Nursery — complete proposed implementation design (`R09-G23`)
**Source:** `G282`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **92.72 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Balance nutrients so tiny living lamps bloom in a coordinated sequence. **Signature animated environment:** flower-like SDF organisms emit phase-locked illumination; Recursive L-systems, instanced leaves, flow network evolution and bioluminescent materials. **Core abstraction:** branching growth grammar.
#### 5.23.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees flower-like sdf organisms emit phase-locked illumination; recursive l-systems, instanced leaves, flow network evolution and bioluminescent materials, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Balance nutrients so tiny living lamps bloom in a coordinated sequence. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `branching growth grammar` computational rules, visual `flower-like SDF organisms emit phase-locked illumination; Recursive L-systems, instanced leaves, flow network evolution and bioluminescent materials` and player control arrangement `Grow/prune branching organisms to satisfy spatial or timing constraints`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.23.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** rewrite L-system symbol grammar with seed, branch budget and nutrient constraints. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Balance nutrients so tiny living lamps bloom in a coordinated sequence. Normalize input into `BiolumeNurseryAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** guide branching structure to supply target nodes or form a defined canopy. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 7 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** graph search over pruning/branch-choice states and growth feasibility. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** exploding node counts, aliasing branches, impossible pruning. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.23.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting flower-like SDF organisms emit phase-locked illumination; Recursive L-systems, instanced leaves, flow network evolution and bioluminescent materials; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable branching growth grammar handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with balance nutrients so tiny living lamps bloom in a coordinated sequence; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative branching growth grammar predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Grow/prune branching organisms to satisfy spatial or timing constraints. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.23.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** tube branch sweep, instanced leaves, procedural subsurface-look tint. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** flower-like SDF organisms emit phase-locked illumination; Recursive L-systems, instanced leaves, flow network evolution and bioluminescent materials. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `BiolumeNurseryScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `BiolumeNurseryParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `d439db526ed2` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.23.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

#### 5.23.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** exploding node counts, aliasing branches, impossible pruning. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `flower-like SDF organisms emit phase-locked illumination; Recursive L-systems, instanced leaves, flow network evolution and bioluminescent materials` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND9_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round9/biolume-nursery/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D2:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND9_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round9/biolume-nursery/D2.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. **Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 24. Prismatic Rapids — complete proposed implementation design (`R09-G24`)
**Source:** `G238`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **92.72 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Redirect colored currents through a field of translucent pylons. **Signature animated environment:** moving spectral ribbons and foam-like particle glints; CPU heightfield/velocity fields, ribbon meshes and transparent-looking GLSL materials. **Core abstraction:** conservative transport grid.
#### 5.24.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees moving spectral ribbons and foam-like particle glints; cpu heightfield/velocity fields, ribbon meshes and transparent-looking glsl materials, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Redirect colored currents through a field of translucent pylons. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `conservative transport grid` computational rules, visual `moving spectral ribbons and foam-like particle glints; CPU heightfield/velocity fields, ribbon meshes and transparent-looking GLSL materials` and player control arrangement `Steer streams through obstacles into deterministic targets`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.24.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** q_next=q+inflow-outflow; Σq drift<=1e-8 in double CPU tests. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Redirect colored currents through a field of translucent pylons. Normalize input into `PrismaticRapidsAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** redirect a finite amount of fluid to specified reservoirs while limiting pollution. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 8 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** deterministic coarse-grid flow search + mass conservation assertions. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** CFL instability, visual physics differing from actual solver. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.24.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting moving spectral ribbons and foam-like particle glints; CPU heightfield/velocity fields, ribbon meshes and transparent-looking GLSL materials; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable conservative transport grid handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with redirect colored currents through a field of translucent pylons; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative conservative transport grid predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Steer streams through obstacles into deterministic targets. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.24.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** animated flow maps on generated terrain and emissive velocity filaments. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** moving spectral ribbons and foam-like particle glints; CPU heightfield/velocity fields, ribbon meshes and transparent-looking GLSL materials. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `PrismaticRapidsScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `PrismaticRapidsParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `05c8352c2cbb` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.24.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

### 25. Orbital Orchard — complete proposed implementation design (`R09-G25`)
**Source:** `G121`, source `Inherited original 200; previously scored`, conceptual score **92.72 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Tune moon orbits so solar light lands on floating garden seeds. **Signature animated environment:** Spherical planets, orbital mechanics and light propagation for seed growth. **Core abstraction:** finite ephemeris puzzle.
#### 5.25.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees spherical planets, orbital mechanics and light propagation for seed growth, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Tune moon orbits so solar light lands on floating garden seeds. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `finite ephemeris puzzle` computational rules, visual `Spherical planets, orbital mechanics and light propagation for seed growth` and player control arrangement `Existing concept input requires game-specific design verification`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.25.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** orbit step is deterministic phase variable; celestial alignment tests in double precision. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Tune moon orbits so solar light lands on floating garden seeds. Normalize input into `OrbitalOrchardAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** reach constellation or orbit alignment within a bounded interaction budget. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 5 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** enumerate discretized configurations with collision and visibility proofs. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** scientific precision claims, shader aliasing. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.25.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting Spherical planets, orbital mechanics and light propagation for seed growth; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable finite ephemeris puzzle handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with tune moon orbits so solar light lands on floating garden seeds; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative finite ephemeris puzzle predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Existing concept input requires game-specific design verification. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.25.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** planet rings, procedural stars, emissive gravitational trails. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** Spherical planets, orbital mechanics and light propagation for seed growth. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `OrbitalOrchardScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `OrbitalOrchardParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `1434b6aea538` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.25.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct finite ephemeris puzzle controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct finite ephemeris puzzle controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct finite ephemeris puzzle controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct finite ephemeris puzzle controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct finite ephemeris puzzle controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct finite ephemeris puzzle controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct finite ephemeris puzzle controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct finite ephemeris puzzle controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct finite ephemeris puzzle controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct finite ephemeris puzzle controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

#### 5.25.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** scientific precision claims, shader aliasing. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `Spherical planets, orbital mechanics and light propagation for seed growth` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND9_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round9/orbital-orchard/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D2:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND9_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round9/orbital-orchard/D2.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad Pro M5, iPadOS 27.2 large-device layout passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D3:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND9_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round9/orbital-orchard/D3.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad A16, iPadOS 26.5 compatibility and slow tier passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
**Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

## 6. Complete Claim–Reason–Evidence AssertionOutlines for all 25 proposed games
Each argument is an INVESTMENT HYPOTHESIS. Claims are contestable. Each of three claims has four reasons and exactly one specific evidence basis. "Proposed verification" means future evidence to collect, not an already observed success; "published comparable" is evidence of the category, NOT of demand for this proposed app. Counterarguments are not suppressed.
### Argument 01: Accordion Isles
#### Claim 1 — Accordion Isles is worth prototyping as a visually differentiated one-price mobile game because compress and stretch modular land strips until destinations touch.
- **Reason 1:** The player has an identifiable and testable decision: Compress and stretch modular land strips until destinations touch.
  - **Evidence 1.1 (type identified):** Specific instance: proposed first-session tutorial and `create a continuous navigable route after rotating and folding room sections` pass/fail contract.
- **Reason 2:** The world has a strong immediate visual signature: elastic landscapes ripple through sharp fold shadows; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows.
  - **Evidence 1.2 (type identified):** Specific instance: shader recipe `procedural architectural panel meshes, normal-mapped-in-code faceting` with deterministic camera and seed to capture later.
- **Reason 3:** The genre has public commercial precedents, but not a guaranteed market.
  - **Evidence 1.3 (type identified):** Public comparable: [Dorfromantik official Steam store](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1455840/) is a genre reference; it does NOT demonstrate this proposal’s sales.
- **Reason 4:** Completeness avoids the empty graphics-demo problem.
  - **Evidence 1.4 (type identified):** Proposed verification: 100 certified levels, genuine solver witnesses and XCUITest win/loss/undo acceptance for `Accordion Isles`.
#### Claim 2 — Accordion Isles is a credible code-only VisualCore production because the core aesthetic, elastic landscapes ripple through sharp fold shadows; hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows, can be built with deterministic shaders and meshes.
- **Reason 1:** The room hinge graph simulation has mathematical semantics independent of textures.
  - **Evidence 2.1 (type identified):** Method/design evidence: `world transforms of connected panels rotate around shared manifold hinges` defines numeric truth; CPU-only unit tests will verify results.
- **Reason 2:** Procedural assets can offer many visual compositions without artists.
  - **Evidence 2.2 (type identified):** Method/design evidence: game seed, mesh compiler, shader parameters and `elastic landscapes ripple through sharp fold shadows; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows` vary under bounded deterministic controls.
- **Reason 3:** The renderer is a known reusable abstraction rather than twenty-five unrelated engines.
  - **Evidence 2.3 (type identified):** Engineering reference: ProjectM-iOS ANGLE/Metal is publicly documented; validate VisualCore local public adapter before implementation.
- **Reason 4:** Visual beauty will be measured in actual frames, not promotional mockups.
  - **Evidence 2.4 (type identified):** Proposed verification: actual GL screenshot goldens, shader compilation logs and D3 endurance for `Accordion Isles`.
#### Claim 3 — Accordion Isles is worth an evidence-gated paid release because its puzzle completeness, device performance and market identity can be tested and falsified before publication.
- **Reason 1:** Commercial risk is bounded by a compact unique core loop.
  - **Evidence 3.1 (type identified):** Design instance: `Compress and stretch modular land strips until destinations touch` and `create a continuous navigable route after rotating and folding room sections` define a concise standalone paid product.
- **Reason 2:** The implementation can be stopped honestly if gameplay is unconvincing.
  - **Evidence 3.2 (type identified):** Proposed falsifier: failing tutorial clarity, engagement test or original-product comparison triggers PIVOT or NO_GO.
- **Reason 3:** The recorded hardware set enables controlled performance decisions.
  - **Evidence 3.3 (type identified):** Owner-supplied devices.md: D1 iPhone15,4; D2 iPad17,3; D3 iPad15,7 on iPadOS 26.5—no results claimed.
- **Reason 4:** A real code-only app avoids the cost and licensing risks of image-generation assets.
  - **Evidence 3.4 (type identified):** Proposed verification: grep dependencies and compiled binary for network/art SDKs; zero manual hero-image files; source-level procedural appearance `procedural architectural panel meshes, normal-mapped-in-code faceting`.
**Counterargument:** Accordion Isles may be a visually appealing but commercially weak shader toy; `unintended paths through seams, camera clipping, deceptive geometry` may also defeat the D3 performance budget. An analogy is not evidence of demand, and no simulated metrics substitute for hardware. **Response/experiment:** show a complete 3-minute new-user win with no assistance, audit all 100 solver witnesses, capture real iOS rendered frames, collect third-party comprehension feedback, compare against existing apps for originality, and reject paid release if actual evidence is weak.
**Decision:** CONSIDER only after all real seed/solver/simulator/device checks; PIVOT if visual readability or originality fails; COMBINE if another title shares the same core goal; NO_GO if D3 cannot sustain a viable quality tier or the product is not enjoyable.

## 7. Full implementation → simulator → device sequential execution protocol
| Gate ID | Exact action | Exit evidence | Device allowed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R09-PREFLIGHT` | Independent previous round8 completed audit and source/skills discovery | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | No real device test |
| `R09-SHARED` | 12 shared features fully specified, implemented and converged; final audit F12 can be deferred to post-device | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | No real device test |
| `R09-GAME` | 25 apps × ten subfeatures fully converged and documented, no placeholders | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | No real device test |
| `R09-SIM` | 25 real targets compiling and all unit, shader and simulator acceptance executed | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | No real device test |
| `R09-LOCK` | Generate verified source SHA, binary catalog, simulator logs, test plan and proof manifests | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | No real device test until verified |
| `R09-D1` | Run ALL 25 signed automation device scripts on D1; 25 result rows | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | D1 only |
| `R09-D2` | Run ALL 25 signed automation device scripts on D2; 25 result rows | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | D2 only |
| `R09-D3` | Run ALL 25 signed automation device scripts on D3; 25 result rows | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | D3 only, NEVER UPDATE |
| `R09-AUDIT` | Converge shared F12, reconcile regressions and final no-ads/legal/graphics audit | source hash, actual command/exit, test report or explicit BLOCKED | Only targeted retests after three runs |
### 7.1 Machine-readable ledger and reliable continuation behavior
```json
{
  "schema": "visualcore.round9.ledger.v1",
  "priorRound": "round8",
  "priorExitVerified": false,
  "repoHead": null,
  "activeFeature": null,
  "sharedFeatures": {
    "R09-F01": "NOT_STARTED"
  },
  "gameFeatures": {
    "R09-G01-01": "NOT_STARTED"
  },
  "implementationLock": {
    "verified": false,
    "sha256": null
  },
  "devices": {
    "D1": {
      "authorized": false,
      "completed": []
    },
    "D2": {
      "authorized": false,
      "completed": []
    },
    "D3": {
      "authorized": false,
      "completed": []
    }
  },
  "nextAction": "VERIFY_PREVIOUS_ROUND",
  "lastError": null
}
```
On every Desktop session: verify real prior-round manifests and source hashes, acquire atomic file lease, inspect git SHA, select first dependency-ready task, invoke installed Spec Kit skills one at a time, inspect produced artifacts, run independent real tests, fsync+os.replace evidence ledger, commit reviewed changes, and prepare accurate next-action prompt. Never ask a Python script to call Claude CLI or private model APIs. The desktop app may pause for usage/tool prompts; never claim continuous execution when it was interrupted.
**Bounded-context retrieval:** Every round file is multiple megabytes. Use a Python heading index, then fetch only the current feature heading, its complete eight prompts, and directly cited contracts. Never load all prior rounds or all commands into a single Claude conversation. Persist feature heading offsets, SHA-256 and next-action cursor in .autonomy state. A truncated snippet is not a completed reading of a feature.

# VisualCore Premium 3D Games — Refined Round 2: 500 Candidates, Code-Only Graphics

**Research baseline:** November 10, 2026 · **Scope:** iOS/iPadOS · **VisualCore path:** existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal · **Business:** one upfront purchase, no advertising, ad SDKs, IAP or subscriptions.

**Scope of evidence:** 500 ideas assessed, **not** 500 researched apps and **not** 500 prototypes. Exactly 200 concepts preserve the previous research matrix; 300 genuinely new concepts were written and scored against declared genre/technical priors. Numeric scores are screening judgments and are not forecasts, experimental results, consumer surveys or audited sales.

## Executive decision: launch a portfolio of experiments, not 25 clones

The screening examined **500** concepts across **62** explicit scoring criteria. **249** pass every proposed code-only/visual/gameplay gate (**20** from the original 200; **229** from the new 300). **25** enter a diverse portfolio shortlist (**4** inherited; **21** newly proposed). Scores favor genuine shader and procedural spectacle, but *a top-25 ranking is a decision to prototype, not a commitment to publish every candidate*.

### Hard requirements

- Graphics originate in procedural geometry, signed distance fields, GLSL ES, parametric meshes, instancing, particles, lighting, algorithms and simulation. There are **zero AI-generated images**, photographic background plates, manually sculpted characters, purchased level art or commissioned texture requirements.
- Use **only the existing VisualCore / projectM-iOS rendering bridge**, through the established ANGLE Metal backend. Do not replace ANGLE, recreate an independent Metal renderer, or ship different backends for each game.
- The visual effect must materially embody a decision in gameplay: steering, folding, redirecting, growing, balancing, tuning or routing. A screensaver with a score counter does not qualify.
- Every game is complete for an upfront $1.99–$4.99 purchase; no ads anywhere, ad SDKs, rewarded screens, analytics ad identifiers, microtransactions, subscriptions, user accounts or live-services infrastructure.
- All physics and visual render loops are bounded and deterministic enough for automation and adaptive quality on D3. This is an *engineering estimate* pending instrumented device tests.
- A portfolio release must satisfy Apple’s originality and spam guidance: no clones of existing games, and no two VisualCore offerings that differ only by visuals or theme. Similar ideas should be merged into a single substantial game.

## 1. Market evidence: what is known, and what is not

- **The mobile gaming market is huge, but not a premium-sales forecast.** Sensor Tower’s [State of Gaming 2026](https://sensortower.com/press/press-release-sensor-tower-state-of-gaming-gaming-drove-52-billion-downloads-82b-iap-revenue-on-mobile-and-12b-premium-revenue-on-steam) reports approximately **$82 billion of 2025 mobile game in-app-purchase revenue** and approximately 52 billion game downloads across mobile, PC and consoles. That $82 billion figure does not represent purchases of upfront-priced iOS games. Gaming downloads per minute are a global scale statistic, not a customer acquisition forecast.

- **People demonstrably pay upfront for some mobile games.** Apple’s [2025 U.S. iPhone top-paid list](https://apps.apple.com/us/iphone/room/6756363168) includes Minecraft, Balatro, Geometry Dash, Bloons TD 6, Stardew Valley, and other recognizable products. Those titles are unusually established competitors; no percentage can be inferred for unknown VisualCore games.

- **Premium, calm, visually distinctive desktop mechanics have audience evidence.** [Tiny Glade](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2198150/Tiny_Glade/) and [Dorfromantik](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1455840/Dorfromantik/) have real positive Steam customer reviews; [Mini Metro](https://store.steampowered.com/app/287980/Mini_Metro/) demonstrates a minimalist routing loop; [Glass Masquerade](https://store.steampowered.com/app/511470/Glass_Masquerade/) shows demand for stylized art puzzles; [Poly Bridge 3](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1850160/Poly_Bridge_3/) shows engagement with construction-physics systems. These are **genre precedents, not proposals to copy**.

- **PC platform context, not sales attribution.** The [October 2026 Steam hardware survey](https://store.steampowered.com/hwsurvey/) reported approximately **93.70% Windows, 3.95% Linux and 2.35% macOS** among respondents. A game working across Windows/macOS/Linux helps demonstrate broad design appeal, but these percentages are neither revenue shares nor iOS conversion metrics.

- **Steam visibility does not equal predictable money.** SteamDB’s [relaxing-game catalog](https://steamdb.info/tag/1654/?min_reviews=500) exposes relative review/follower/peak-player measures; pricing and review counts are public but unit sales cannot be inferred reliably by simply multiplying reviews by a constant. This portfolio therefore does not invent per-candidate sales numbers.

### A platform-portability precedent (verified from product listings)

| Comparable PC product | Verified lesson | Porting caveat |
|---|---|---|
| [[Tiny Glade](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2198150/Tiny_Glade/)] | Procedural diorama creation has strong positive reception; its official Steam store lists Windows, macOS and Linux requirements | Its rendering budgets, assets, controls and developer recognition do not automatically carry to iPhone |
| [[Mini Metro](https://store.steampowered.com/app/287980/Mini_Metro/)] | A small visual ruleset can deliver meaningful strategy without elaborate character animation | Its map-driven 2D interaction differs from three-dimensional spectacle |
| [[Dorfromantik](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1455840/Dorfromantik/)] | Geometry and systems can deliver relaxation with decision-making | Procedural 3D landscapes need device-level simplification |
| [[Glass Masquerade](https://store.steampowered.com/app/511470/Glass_Masquerade/)] | Art-led premium puzzles can accumulate a dedicated audience | A new 3D optics game must not mimic protected stained-glass motifs or arrangements |
| [[Poly Bridge 3](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1850160/Poly_Bridge_3/)] | Physics construction can support complete, rule-driven play | A phone needs shorter stages, cheaper simulation and touch-first controls |

## 2. Copyright, App Store policy and the danger of indistinguishable games

The [U.S. Copyright Office](https://www.copyright.gov/register/tx-games.html) says that a game idea or playing method is not itself protected by copyright, but specific artwork, text and other expression can be. This is not a license to reuse game code, exact levels, names, trademarks, audio, distinctive visual identity or copied marketing. Open-source licenses must be audited if any source is considered, and no code from other games is required for the shortlisted titles.

Apple [App Review Guidelines 4.1 and 4.3](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/) flag copycats and repeated near-identical apps. **The goal is not to flood the App Store with 25 shader reskins.** For every candidate the product team must document one mechanic, one content structure and one user experience that differs materially from every other shipped app; merge overlapping ideas when they do not pass the distinctiveness review.

## 3. All 62 criteria, rubric and score calculation

Each criterion is rated on a **1–5 ordinal judgment scale** (1 = weak, 3 = plausible, 5 = strong). Decimal ratings indicate heuristic prioritization, *not measured accuracy*. Original 200 candidates retain their earlier 50 and 12 ratings; 300 new concepts receive scores from their old-category reference averages plus documented text/trait modifiers (see the included code). No row has its own directly observed purchase conversion data.

**Commercial/engineering subtotal:** `C = 20 × Σ(criterion_rating × original_weight × group_multiplier) / Σ(original_weight × group_multiplier)`, with multipliers Market 0.78, Competition 0.86, Premium 1.00, Experience 1.22, Engineering 1.29.

**Visual subtotal:** `V = 20 × Σ(visual_rating × visual_weight) / Σ(visual_weight)`. **Final screening score:** `0.30 × C + 0.70 × V`. The 70% weighting prioritizes code-generatable spectacle. **Eligibility is assessed independently before shortlisting**; an unqualified game cannot win by a high weighted average.

| V05 | Fully programmatic geometry and materials | 6 | 4.45 | Everything hero-quality can be created in code with procedural generators |
| V06 | Zero image-generation requirements | 11 | 4.90 | No OpenAI/Claude/raster prompt generation needed for final art |
